newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Russian deputy PM in Sofia - still in cabinet?.
newsitem.headline: Russian deputy PM in Sofia - still in cabinet?.

text.p: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Oleg Lobov, who heard of Tuesday's Moscow government reshuffle while on a visit to Bulgaria, said he would wait and see if he was in the cabinet but reassured his hosts his signature was still valid.

"The document says that (Prime Minister Viktor) Chernomyrdin has to submit proposals in one week for changes in the government, including resignations and new appointments. It is not important whether I will work or not because Russia will remain," Lobov told a news conference in Sofia.
A decree from President Boris Yeltsin said the number of deputy prime ministers would be cut from the current figure of nine.
Lobov and his Bulgarian hosts signed a protocol on energy and trade issues, preparing issues for the agenda of an intergovernmental committee meeting planned for June.

"The signature on this protocol is legal and, besides, it is signed not only by Lobov, but also by the officials that accompanied me on this visit, including (Gazprom president) Mr Rem Vyahirev, who is head of a company and will not be affected by any decision of the president," Lobov said.
"We have to keep on working and I will keep on working in any post to preserve the good relations between our two countries," said Lobov, who was due to return to Moscow later on Tuesday.
